I'm not an expert, so please take what I say with a grain of salt. If this is a recurring issue for you, then you should probably seek out a psychiatrist if you have the coverage with your health insurance. Anti-depressants are an option, but not usually a solution in themselves. It's best to find a shrink that offers counseling, or can recommend a counselor to help you through your social anxiety. Drugs are a stop-gap that will allow you to easier develop your sociability, and the two work better together.

I sometimes have anxiety as a side-effect of my medication. It's not social anxiety, but more of a spontaneous, irrational type of anxiety. When this happens I prefer to clear my mind and take a short break from whatever I'm doing, but this probably wouldn't have the same effect in a social setting. I think the healthiest thing to do would be to find a comfortable outlet to socialize with others in real life and examine possible sources of general anxiety in your life (school, work, family, etc.).

Meditation and benzos(although if you're going under sedation talk to your doc and dentist about the benzos first). If things get really bad I find a low dose takes the edge off just enough to be able to use things like breathing and meditation to calm down.

This might sound weird, but I give myself half an hour to worry and be fearful and criticize and analyze my every thought and action every morning. 15 minutes if i am really pressed for time. After that, I go about my day. If I am feeling bad about something, I write it down. There is no way to tell yourself to stop feeling the way that you do. But I tell myself I can focus on whatever it is in that half hour. It seems to help some. I take some deep breaths and do my best to continue on.

I also have begun trying to meditate for the same time at night. I start my day with going through my woes, so I deserve to end it on a clear note. It has been helping me get better sleep.
